signals.evidence: In Baram, community leaders expressed lack of trust in politicians and the army, stating they told unrealistic stories and promised a quiet, secure border that did not materialize in reality.
In Abdon/Maaleh Yosef, there is concern that the army is not telling the truth.
In Liman/Matte Asher, message to IDF: 'Do not tell stories!'
In Baram, farmers report limited number of armored field protection booths (מיגוניות) relative to the scope of agricultural land.
In Baram, there is a shortage of protected spaces for educational and social activities; no suitable public space exists.
In Goren/Maaleh Yosef, many residents lack individual safe rooms (ממ"דים); public shelters are not in optimal condition; some residents have shelters that are far from them.
In Abdon/Maaleh Yosef, not all elderly have individual safe rooms (ממ"דים); public shelters are far away; no possibility to reach shelters in time.
In Abdon/Maaleh Yosef, additional armored field protection booths (מיגוניות) are needed.
In Liman/Matte Asher, there are known protection gaps; all are in process of receiving solutions.
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, there are protection gaps; elderly lack protection.
In Matta/Maaleh Yosef - Baram: families without individual safe rooms (mamad)
In Pesuta - Baram: 55% of homes without protective infrastructure (migunim); one shelter unsuitable for use

In Alkosh/Maaleh Yosef - Baram: elderly population struggling to reach protected areas; approximately 70% have individual safe rooms; 10% have underground shelters; total 8 public shelters with 3 requiring repairs
In Horfish - Baram: 30% without protective infrastructure; gap closed in all public institutions and public spaces
In Kibbutz Eilon/Matte Asher - Baram: shelter conditions poor - old systems, stuffy; no protection in local clinic
In Baram, informal activities began today; HFC volunteer corps (צח"י) training and volunteer reinforcement are underway.
In Abdon/Maaleh Yosef, informal activities are taking place; community coordinator is recruiting volunteers.
In Batzet/Matte Asher - Baram: active Home Front Command volunteers; soldier-teachers and army education core present
In Pesuta - Baram: volunteer network exists; many volunteers but weak coordination; not all arriving and only one trained
In Alkosh/Maaleh Yosef - Baram: Home Front Command includes only the coordinator with no additional functionaries; limited enrichment activities for children
In Pesuta - Baram: decompression workshops and learning center for high school students
In Baram, there is concern about business collapse, specifically a pizzeria.
In Baram, there is a gap in educators; proposal to fill the gap with the help of reserve soldiers.
In Goren/Maaleh Yosef, the narrative is to stay, though accompanied by difficulties.
In Abdon/Maaleh Yosef, residents are not leaving; community coordinator is recruiting volunteers; women's evening and activities for adults are held.

In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, community resilience is expressed in the willingness to enable what is possible without distraction; most of the population has returned to the settlement; there is a young functioning population; discourse of coping.
In Pesuta - Baram: overall resilience but political instability affecting it; people in emergency routine but more freely; there is learning and training for essential workers and medical staff
In Goren/Maaleh Yosef, there is variation in reports about going out to work.
In Batzet/Matte Asher - Baram: beginning to enter emergency routine; activities for younger ages operating in cycles due to lack of suitable shelters
In Horfish - Baram: full emergency routine; private businesses opening; council-related matters showing policy hardening
In Yaara/Maaleh Yosef - Baram: silence in the street, almost no vehicles driving; no open businesses; those who remained are sheltering; people only go out if necessary
In Goren/Maaleh Yosef, there is an increase in the number of calls to the 106 emergency hotline.
In Goren/Maaleh Yosef, elderly population faces distress; difficulty reaching safe rooms; sometimes injured.
In Batzet/Matte Asher - Baram: strong leadership and cooperation among different role-holders
In Abdon/Maaleh Yosef, expansion of activities for children is underway.
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, there is basic youth activity.
In Liman/Matte Asher, there is a sense of loss of trust toward politicians and military personnel.
In Liman/Matte Asher, the central distress is lack of activities for children.
In Batzet/Matte Asher - Baram: children and youth at home using Zoom with limited success; difficulty operating educational frameworks
In Kibbutz Eilon/Matte Asher - Baram: informal education - activity exists but relatively limited because instructors are partly not kibbutz residents and have not returned
In Yaara/Maaleh Yosef - Baram: no frameworks; informal education for some kindergarten and early elementary children
In Liman/Matte Asher, those who can afford it have individual safe rooms (ממ"דים).
In Matta/Maaleh Yosef - Baram: extensive protective infrastructure in public spaces
In Batzet/Matte Asher - Baram: light renovation of shelter for educational activities
In Liman/Matte Asher, there is difficulty protecting farmers' security.
In Liman/Matte Asher, HFC volunteer corps (צח"י) overall functions well.
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, there is a community readiness unit (כיתת כוננות).
In Matta/Maaleh Yosef - Baram: community coordinator working at full capacity
In Horfish - Baram: authority broadcasting resilience and high control in the community; strong community
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, there is a sense of fatigue and erosion from the ongoing situation.
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, community communication exists without evidence of toxic discourse.
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, there is good relationship with the council and Home Front Command.
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, HFC volunteer corps (צח"י) is not operating at full capacity.

In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, elderly and those with special needs feel there is no 'father and mother' - no entity within the community that has a complete picture of elderly and people with disabilities.
In Alkosh/Maaleh Yosef - Baram: community lacks the community backbone - recommendation to establish welfare coordination for leadership and joint community activity dimensions
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, there is a lack of precise mapping of the entire population because HFC is not operating at full capacity.

In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, there is a lack of connection between welfare services and this population - elderly, urban residents, families with children with special needs, and other populations including women whose family members are in military service.
In Even Menahem/Maaleh Yosef, residents describe themselves as 'mentally ill people living here'; feeling of abandonment; 'we are the periphery of the periphery'.
In Kibbutz Eilon/Matte Asher - Baram: feeling of broken community cohesion following evacuation in Iron Swords War; residents more independent and less engaged in community activities
In Matta/Maaleh Yosef - Baram: couples from the public shelter (which serves as a youth club) conducted rehearsals for a memorial evening of song in memory of Mati Kaspi
In Matta/Maaleh Yosef - Baram: community cohesion strengthened significantly
In Matta/Maaleh Yosef - Baram: need for sewage infrastructure repair
In Pesuta - Baram: clubs for elderly and special needs closed; difficult to visit them
In Horfish - Baram: no activity even in public shelters
In Kibbutz Eilon/Matte Asher - Baram: need to restore medical/clinic response
In Batzet/Matte Asher - Baram: farmers working and people going out to work
In Batzet/Matte Asher - Baram: complexities of substance use (drugs and alcohol) discovered among youth
In Alkosh/Maaleh Yosef - Baram: general apathy expressed in lack of volunteering for leisure activities and community engagement; no community cohesion; no inspiring leadership for action
In Horfish - Baram: loneliness; frameworks not working for elderly, women, and special populations; everything cancelled with only minimal activity via Zoom
In Pesuta - Baram: difficulty reaching all residents for welfare services; informal activities conducted by education department
In Alkosh/Maaleh Yosef - Baram: residents obedient regarding policy aspects and Home Front Command directives
In Horfish - Baram: requests for social services - assistance with economic support for small business owners and parents with children
In Kibbutz Eilon/Matte Asher - Baram: many essential workers and feeling of uncertainty because there are no answers and no solutions for children of essential workers
In Baram, elderly population is receiving community support.
In Pesuta - Baram: student council activities
In Pesuta - Baram: elderly experiencing loneliness and difficulty
